+# #769 - Part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks
+
+## What was decided
+
+Two perpendicular picks - an edge (or two points) for +Y and one for
++X - now define the setup's part alignment outright, in full 3D:
+`pick::align_from_axes` builds the frame with the primary axis kept
+exactly, the secondary orthogonalized against it, and +Z landing on
+the picks' cross (the right-hand rule). The panel that was #557's
+in-plane turn applies it (renamed `AlignPartFromAxes`); with one axis
+picked the twist about it is free, so the work plane still carries the
+turn (`turn_in_plane` unchanged, kept for its single-pick callers).
+The pivot is the parts' centre; the ORIGIN is deliberately out of
+scope (the work offset is placed separately, exactly as before).
+
+## Why
+
+The user's pick round (a 43 mm edge running down -Z picked as +Y, a
+31.5 mm edge running -X picked as +X) carries complete frame
+information that `turn_in_plane` threw away: it can only spin about
+the work plane's normal, so an out-of-plane pick was refused ("runs
+(nearly) along the work plane's normal") and the user was sent to a
+plane-first workaround. The user's law: the two directions define the
+axes, and where they run decides where +Z goes - no workaround, the
+core flow must accept it. Mathematically the two directions compose
+as a plain basis construction (`quat_from_axes` + conjugate), the same
+building blocks the 3-2-1 geometry flow already uses.
+
+## Considered and dropped
+
+- **Keeping the left-handed refusal** for in-plane pick pairs: with
+  full 3D freedom both picks are always honourable literally; refusing
+  would again throw away information the user gave. A left-handed pair
+  now lands the part on its head - visible, undoable, and exactly what
+  the picks said. Pinned deliberately in
+  `a_left_handed_pair_is_honoured_literally_not_refused`.
+- **A max-skew refusal** (picks not perpendicular enough): the
+  secondary lands within the skew it came with, reported by the
+  landing proof; orthogonalization is the standard answer, not a
+  refusal. Only (anti)parallel picks within 1 degree refuse, by name.
+- **Setting the origin in the same step**: explicitly deferred by the
+  user ("definition des nullpunktes ist dabei erstmal egal") - the
+  work offset flow stays the one place origins are placed.
+- **A new panel**: same rows, same picks, same flip toggles - only the
+  meaning grew. The words under Apply now say which case applies
+  ("turns N about Z" in-plane, "aligns the part" full 3D).
+
+## What it would cost to change later
+
+Every later alignment flow (origin picking, mate-like snaps) composes
+on `align_from_axes`' contract: primary exact, secondary
+orthogonalized, Z from the cross, pivot the parts' centre. Changing
+the composition order or the literal-honouring law means re-deriving
+the pins in `tests/align_axes.rs` (9 tests) and the UI pin
+`two_picks_with_an_upright_edge_align_the_part_in_full_3d`.

+# #771 - Two orientation dropdowns, one section everywhere
+
+## What was decided
+
+The five scattered alignment sections collapsed into ONE section with
+TWO dropdowns - "Plane orientation" (Axes default, Points, Face,
+Manual, Cylinder angle) and "Orientation point" (model box, stock
+box, manual vertex) - mounted identically on the Setups overview and
+each setup's Settings page. The existing row functions draw verbatim
+as the expanded content; the completing work is the cylinder angle
+(one curved-wall pick names the axis from the wall's facet normals;
+it lands on a chosen world axis, turned by an angle about it) and the
+per-setup WCS origin placement keeping the rotation.
+
+## Why
+
+The user's law: two dropdowns, the matching settings expanding below
+each, existing functions reused, the missing possibilities completed
+- and the section everywhere a setup's orientation is edited (the
+all-setups view and each single setup's page), looking the same. The
+cylinder reading had to be the wall's own geometry rather than a
+two-centroid trick, because a plain bore or cylinder welds into ONE
+wall whose centre of mass carries no direction: every facet normal
+of a cylinder wall is perpendicular to its axis, so the first
+normal crossed with the most perpendicular one names the axis
+exactly, and every other normal verifies it - a mixed patch is
+refused by name, never silently misread (the prime directive).
+
+## Considered and dropped
+
+- **Two wall picks naming the axis by their centroids' run**: only
+  works for stepped bores (two separate walls); a plain cylinder is
+  one welded wall, so both picks would read the same centre and
+  refuse. Dropped for the facet-normal reading, which needs one pick
+  and any wall.
+- **A least-squares / PCA cylinder fit**: the axis as the normals'
+  null direction is exact for a tessellated wall and cheap; a full
+  fit buys nothing here and adds failure modes.
+- **A new origin command**: `SetWcsOrigin` gained a `for_setup`
+  constructor instead (the active-setup behaviour unchanged); the
+  rotation is kept because the frame comes from the plane side - the
+  two dropdowns are the 3-2-1 setup split.
+- **Marking rows behind a collapsed dropdown as "shown"**: the #664
+  law already covers it - a method whose row is not drawn is a row
+  off screen; the draft disarms exactly as if the page was left.
+
+## What it would cost to change later
+
+The cylinder reading's contract (primary normals, verification
+tolerance `NORMAL_TOL`) is pinned by `tests/orient_dropdowns.rs`
+(landings on X/Y/Z, the angle swing, the refusals); the section's
+mount points and the dropdown semantics by the rewritten structural
+twin and `switch_plane_method` in the disarm suites. The temp-slot
+law (one id read OUTSIDE the horizontal - a child Ui names a
+different slot) is the one that bit: any future dropdown in this code
+base must read its id once, outside the layout closure.
